newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says may consider U.S. wheat if price right.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says may consider U.S. wheat if price right.

text.p: Egypt's main commodities buyer said on Friday he may ask American traders to supply 50,000 tonnes of soft red or soft white wheat if their grain prices are lower than those offered by Australian traders.
Egypt tendered earlier this week for 50,000 tonnes of soft red French wheat or soft white Australian wheat. Friday was the closing date for the bids.
"The Australians are offering attractive prices but if the Americans come through with lower prices, we'll invite them to tender as well," Samir el-Shakankiri told Reuters.
He did not specify the price the Australians were offering but said it was lower than current American prices.
"We'll wait and see what American bourse close at...then we'll decide," he said.
Shakankiri also denied rumours that he had bought 1.2 million tonnes of Australian wheat overnight. "We have not bought such a large amount of Australian wheat. This news is not true," he said.
